messages.author: ed8d9f4a4c19d66c
messages.subject: Fidgeting
parts:
Hello all, 

Does anyone use an accelerometer to monitor fidgeting? Could you help me with my analysis? 
I am monitoring fidgeting from 8 am to 2 pm on my testing day, and the accelerometer was worn on both ankles and right wrist. Participants were asked to avoid fidgeting during this time; if they did, I hoped the accelerometer could detect the frequency. 
However, after running the analysis on GGIR, I could not get the average acceleration value (no value at all). On the calibration status, there are two error messages.

1. recalibration attempted with all available data, but possibly not good enough: Check calibration error variable to verify this.
2. recalibration not done because not enough points on all sides of the sphere

Can anyone help me, please? I have no idea what to do next.

Thank you for your help.

Liza

messages.author: 4b9dc262ec278dc5
messages.subject: Re: Fidgeting
parts:
Hi Norliza,

As explained in the documentation, the performance of the auto-calibration algorithm depends on the number of non-movement periods found in the data and the variation of the accelerometer orientation. If the recording is too short, as I think is your case, the algorithm is expected to perform less and that explains the warning (not error) messages that you are getting. You can go to the data quality report within the results/QC folder to verify the initial and final calibration error and decide on whether this error is sufficiently low for your purposes.

When you say that you could not get the average acceleration value, what do you mean? Please specify what GGIR reports or files you are looking at. In the case that you are looking at the part 2 reports, consider adjusting the criteria to consider a valid day (includedaycrit) to be a meaningful number for your study protocol. The parameter includedaycrit is 16 by default, requiring 16 valid hours in a day to consider it valid. If your recording only expands to a few hours, then you need to consider reducing that threshold to get the data for that specific day.

Best,
Jairo
